To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the excitation of the resonators with femtosecond laser pulses leads to a significant increase in the sensitivity and the accuracy of the measurements of the parameters of these pulses.

the generation of electromagnetic waves in resonators with electro-optic crystals is possible with ultrashort pulses of radiation with a duration of 10−15 s and that the measurement of the characteristics of ultrashort pulses can be carried out using the same method.

the generation of electromagnetic pulses in a resonator with electrooptic crystals excited by a laser pulse is described by the equations of nonlinear optics, that the generation of the electromagnetic pulse is a nonlinear process, that the parameters of the electromagnetic pulse are determined by the initial conditions, and that the parameters of a laser pulse can be measured by the method of nonlinear interferometry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation and detection of ultrashort electromagnetic pulses.
the study of the interaction of laser radiation with matter, in particular the interaction of ultrashort light pulses with the medium.
the generation and detection of ultrashort optical pulses, and with the use of ultrashort pulses to probe the dynamics of condensed matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study has shown that the use of the method of ultrashort pulse excitation is very promising for the investigation of resonators with electrooptic crystals.

the theory of the generation and propagation of ultrashort light pulses is still in its infancy, and that there are many problems that have not been solved and many questions that have not been answered.

, while the use of ultrashort pulses to excite resonator systems containing electrooptic crystals is an important new method for the measurement of the pulse parameters and for the generation of electromagnetic waves, the method has not yet reached a stage of maturity where it can be applied routinely to a wide range of problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrooptic effect is a convenient tool for the generation of ultrashort pulses, but the use of this effect for the measurement of pulse parameters is limited to a few special cases.
it is possible to generate ultrashort pulses with a duration of 10 ^{-11} s and to measure the duration of ultrashort pulses of the order 10 ^{-10} s.
we have shown that the use of ultrashort pulses in the measurement of electrooptic parameters is a very powerful method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the generation of the radiation in the resonator and the measurement of the pulse duration are possible only in the case when the pulse duration of the exciting laser pulse is less than or equal to the duration of the pulse of the generated radiation.

the generation of the radiation is determined by the properties of the crystal and the resonator, while the measurement of the pulse parameters is determined by the characteristics of the crystal, the resonator, and the detection system.
the use of electrooptic resonators allows one to obtain information about the temporal structure of the exciting pulses, and to measure the parameters of these pulses with an accuracy of up to 1%.
